description: A Computer Science junior with a background in competitive programming and a professional interest in cybersecurity and systems vulnerability research.

nodes.title: OS Foundations & System Structure
nodes.description: An exploration of the core services and hierarchical structures of modern operating systems, including the distinction between kernel and user modes.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Because this student has strong_prior_exposure, we move directly to core system structures without introductory C/Systems scaffolding.

nodes.title: Advanced Kernel Architecture Tradeoffs
nodes.description: A comparative analysis of monolithic, microkernel, and hybrid kernel designs, focusing on performance tradeoffs and security implications.
nodes.personalizationRationale: This student's strong_prior_exposure enables an advanced look at architectural tradeoffs that go beyond the basic syllabus floor.
Core process abstraction is mandatory for all students, but we leverage this student's strong_prior_exposure to cover basic IPC efficiently.
nodes.description: Understanding the process lifecycle, PCB structures, and fundamental Inter-Process Communication (IPC) through shared memory and message passing.
nodes.title: Process Lifecycle & Fundamental IPC
High-Performance IPC Engineering
nodes.personalizationRationale: Given the student's strong_prior_exposure, this node explores the engineering challenges of building high-throughput message-passing systems.
nodes.description: An in-depth look at high-performance IPC mechanisms, including socket programming nuances and shared memory synchronization efficiency.

nodes.title: Threads & CPU Scheduling Criteria
nodes.description: Examination of threading models (User vs Kernel), standard libraries (Pthreads), and the core criteria used for CPU scheduling.
nodes.personalizationRationale: As a student with strong_prior_exposure, core threading models are covered at an accelerated pace to make room for complex scheduling theory.

nodes.title: Advanced Multi-Core Scheduling Strategy
nodes.personalizationRationale: Strong_prior_exposure allows this student to tackle the complexities of scheduling in modern multi-core environments.
nodes.description: Detailed study of multi-processor and multi-core scheduling, including affinity, load balancing, and real-time scheduling constraints.

nodes.personalizationRationale: Required midterm review assessment to verify the student's strong_prior_exposure translates to exam readiness for the week-8 milestone.
nodes.description: A comprehensive review of chapters 1-5 and a practice assessment to ensure mastery of foundations, processes, and scheduling.
nodes.title: Midterm Review Checkpoint (Ch. 1-5)
Synchronization Primitives & Critical Sections
nodes.description: Practical application of mutex locks, semaphores, and monitors to solve the critical section problem.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Synchronization is a core requirement; we build on this student's strong_prior_exposure to implement standard primitives.

nodes.description: Exploring lock-free data structures, atomic operations, and the implementation of custom synchronization primitives for high-concurrency environments.
nodes.personalizationRationale: For a student with strong_prior_exposure, this node investigates modern concurrency techniques beyond basic semaphores.
nodes.title: Concurreny Beyond Mutexes: Lock-Free Design

nodes.description: Formal characterization of deadlocks and the study of prevention, avoidance (Banker's Algorithm), and detection techniques.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Required floor content on deadlock theory, delivered without scaffolding due to the student's strong_prior_exposure.
nodes.title: Deadlock Characterization & Avoidance

nodes.description: Case studies of deadlock scenarios in distributed systems and large-scale resource allocation environments.
nodes.personalizationRationale: This student's strong_prior_exposure permits a broader look at how deadlock manifests in complex, distributed architectures.
nodes.title: Deadlock in Distributed Systems

nodes.personalizationRationale: Memory management is a core requirement; the student's strong_prior_exposure helps them grasp page table structures quickly.
nodes.description: Examination of memory addressing, paging, segmentation, and the implementation of demand paging in virtual memory systems.
nodes.title: Physical & Virtual Memory Management

nodes.personalizationRationale: Utilizing the student's strong_prior_exposure to evaluate the performance impact of page replacement at the system level.
nodes.description: Analysis of advanced page replacement algorithms and the hardware-software interface required to minimize thrashing.
nodes.title: Performance Analysis of Paging Systems

nodes.description: Overview of I/O hardware, kernel I/O subsystems, and the design and implementation of file system structures.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Core capstone material on I/O and files, requiring no extra scaffolding for this student with strong_prior_exposure.
nodes.title: I/O Systems & File Storage Implementation

nodes.description: Advanced exploration of Log-Structured File Systems (LFS) and optimization techniques for modern Solid State Drives (SSDs).
